candidates.title: Draft order updates from changing store data

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare customer-facing order status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: customer-facing status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently

ease.reason: A student can draft from operator-supplied sample order facts, but no implementation reference is attached.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: online shops may pay for clearer order updates; this request establishes no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft from synthetic status changes, while live data access and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed trigger could prepare drafts, but a person must verify changing facts and approve every message.

evidence.reason: The request names customer-facing updates and incomplete or changing data, but not frequency, fields or implementation.

candidates.reason: Assessed a bounded draft-from-sample-data experiment. Rejected as a duplicate of recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6: both target online shops and handling customer support communications; its provisional mean is also below 6.

candidates.title: Prepare restaurant order arrival alerts

demandEvidence.chore: Build a system that notifies a restaurant when a new website order is placed.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: automated restaurant order notification system using Make.com

ease.reason: A synthetic order can support a simple alert mock, but no supplied building reference supports the trigger or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: restaurants taking web orders may pay for alerts; this request establishes no paying customer.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can format a test alert, but live order access and WhatsApp delivery are unsupported here.

autonomy.reason: A proposed event-to-alert loop is narrow, though a person must configure access and verify each destination.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly names restaurant web-order notifications, but gives no frequency, detailed fields or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: Assessed a narrow synthetic order-to-alert experiment; provisional mean 4.2 is below the threshold of 6. No supplied implementation reference supports the trigger or WhatsApp delivery, and the request does not establish repeat demand.

candidates.title: Review unnecessary trusted root authorities

demandEvidence.chore: Identify root signing authorities a system may not need and review a proposed block list.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: After the recent eMudhra CA incident, I wondered why my system trusts over 150 root signing authorities, most of which I don't need? I decided to scratch my own itch and make a tool to block the long

ease.reason: A read-only report over synthetic trust entries is a small mock, but no supplied reference documents certificate-store parsing.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: security consultants might pay for trust-list review, but the post describes the maker’s own itch and proves no buyer.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test could flag user-selected entries in a synthetic list; real certificate formats and safe deployment remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed scan can flag entries, but a security professional must verify every change; automated blocking could disrupt secure connections.

evidence.reason: The Show HN excerpt names excess trusted roots and a blocking tool, but is truncated and gives no external demand or workflow detail.

candidates.reason: Assessed a read-only synthetic-list review experiment. Provisional mean 18/5 = 3.6, below threshold; the post describes a maker’s own itch rather than an external professional-services request, and live blocking carries security risk.
